label: Original-phase input of p/q/g (or 3/2/s/t/i after an early letter e/f/r/n/c/h/o/k)
explanation: Almost all of its activation (99.9%) falls in the original (input) phase. It never fires at t=0 or on <DEL>, and almost never in the copy phase. It is driven by the current input token: p (rate 35%, 28% of mass), q, and g are strongest, followed by 3, 2, s, t, i, with weaker firing on y/1/b/l. Activation is higher at middle positions (orig_idx 3-6) and on the first occurrence of a token (90% of mass). It is also higher when earlier tokens include letters like e/f/r/n/c/h (first_tok and prev2_tok lift up to about 2x). The strongest examples are p, at about 0.3, after prefixes like e r ... or e d n .... The same token gives graded, context-dependent magnitudes, which suggests a linear mix of current-token identity and accumulated hidden-state context; a boolean predicate tops out around dev F1 0.6. Dev: P 0.50, R 0.85, F1 0.63, mass recall 0.92.
